Code Tit. 27 Ch. 15, NAIC Model #808 as adopted, filed with ALDOI) read with the Standard Valuation Law (Model #820) and the current NAIC Valuation Manual (VM-20, VM-A, VM-C, VM-M); the Arizona, California and Connecticut nonforfeiture statutes are re-read each January for amendments to the nonforfeiture interest rate basis and the operative CSO mortality table

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Nonforfeiture basis summary by issue-year cohort, a worked adjusted-premium example per plan code, the CSV floor test result and the Exhibit 5 tie-out, producible for an ALDOI financial examiner or an NAIC Financial Analysis Handbook Level 1 request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Statutory Reporting logs the request; the Valuation Actuary drafts the calculation response, the Appointed Actuary approves it, and Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes a nonforfeiture shortfall before it goes to ALDOI or a non-domiciliary department

checklist.step: Cut and lock the certificate-level valuation in-force extract
actions: Ask the Policy Admin Ops Lead to freeze policy-administration postings for the valuation date and confirm the freeze time in writing before extracting.

Run the valuation extract for all Group Life certificates carrying guaranteed values: certificate number, master policy number, plan code, issue date, issue age, sex/composite indicator, face amount, mode and gross premium, paid-to date, situs state, writing company NAIC co-code, current guaranteed cash value and outstanding policy loan.
Record the extract row count, total face amount and a file hash on the valuation control sheet and store the extract read-only in the enterprise data warehouse under the valuation date.
Reject and re-cut the extract if issue dates or paid-to dates contain nulls — a null issue date silently mis-assigns the governing nonforfeiture mortality table.
checklist.done: a frozen, hashed certificate-level extract exists for the valuation date with recorded control totals and no null issue or paid-to dates.

checklist.step: Cohort the in-force by the nonforfeiture standard that governs each issue year
actions: Split the extract into issue-year cohorts and assign each its governing nonforfeiture mortality table: 1980 CSO for pre-2009 issues, 2001 CSO for 2009-2019 issues and 2017 CSO for issues on or after 1 January 2020, with the smoker/non-smoker or composite variant as filed.

Record for each cohort the sex-distinct versus unisex basis, age last birthday versus age nearest birthday, and any state — Alabama, Arizona, California or Connecticut — that mandates a different table than the domiciliary standard.
Cross-check every cohort assignment against the approved form filing held by the Product Filing Specialist so the valuation basis matches the basis certified in that form's actuarial memorandum.
Write the cohort table (issue-year range, plan code, table, age basis, interest rate) onto the valuation control sheet and have the Chief Actuary initial it before any model run.
checklist.done: every certificate sits in an issue-year cohort with a named mortality table and age basis that matches its approved filing.

checklist.step: Derive and freeze the calendar-year nonforfeiture and valuation interest rates
actions: Take the calendar-year statutory valuation interest rate for each plan type and guarantee duration from the Standard Valuation Law dynamic formula using the published Moody's Corporate Bond Yield Average Monthly Average Corporates for the reference period.
Compute the nonforfeiture interest rate as 125% of that valuation interest rate rounded to the nearest 0.25% and show the arithmetic step by step on the rate worksheet rather than pasting the answer.
Confirm the result against the NAIC's published calendar-year valuation and nonforfeiture interest rate table and document any difference before it is used.

Freeze the rates for the calendar year, date and initial the worksheet, and circulate it to the Reserving Actuary and the Product / Filing Actuary so pricing, filing and valuation all run on the same basis.
checklist.done: the calendar-year valuation and nonforfeiture interest rates are derived, agreed to the published NAIC table and frozen on a dated worksheet.

checklist.step: Load the frozen basis and in-force into the valuation model
actions: Open the production Group Life valuation run in the actuarial modeling platform and point the model point file at the frozen extract path and hash.

Load the CSO table set, the frozen nonforfeiture and valuation interest rates and the plan-level product parameters, then confirm the model version tag matches the version approved in the model governance repository.
Run the model's reconciliation report and check that model point count and total face amount tie exactly to the extract control totals recorded on the control sheet.
Stop and escalate to the Model Risk Manager if the model version, table set or rate file differs from the approved configuration instead of overriding it inside the run.
checklist.done: the run is configured on the approved model version and frozen basis, with model point counts and face amounts tied to the extract control totals.

checklist.step: Compute minimum cash surrender values by the adjusted premium method
actions: Run the nonforfeiture routine to produce, per certificate and duration, the present value of future guaranteed benefits less the present value of future adjusted premiums on the cohort's nonforfeiture mortality and interest basis.

Confirm the expense allowance inside the adjusted premium follows the statutory formula — the 1.25% of the amount of insurance component, the per-thousand component and the permitted first-year nonforfeiture net level premium component — and print those components separately rather than as one netted figure.
Extract the minimum paid-up nonforfeiture benefit and the extended term insurance amount and period alongside the cash values so the default nonforfeiture option can be tested.
Export the per-certificate minimum value table to the enterprise data warehouse keyed on certificate number and duration.
Hand the Chief Actuary a worked example per plan code showing PV benefits, PV adjusted premiums, expense allowance components and the resulting minimum value.
checklist.done: per-certificate minimum cash surrender, paid-up and extended term values exist for every duration, with a component-level worked example per plan code.

checklist.step: Compare modelled minimums to the guaranteed values printed on the contract
actions: Pull the Table of Guaranteed Values held against each plan code in the policy administration system and in the approved form held by the Product Filing Specialist.
Join the modelled statutory minimum to the printed guaranteed value at each duration and compute printed minus statutory minimum per certificate per duration.

List every row where the printed guaranteed value is below the statutory minimum — these are contract-level nonforfeiture deficiencies, not rounding, and go straight to the exception log the same day.
Summarise the comparison by plan code and issue-year cohort with row count and worst-case deficiency and send it to the Valuation Actuary and the Product / Filing Actuary.
checklist.done: every plan code has a duration-by-duration comparison of printed guarantees to statutory minimums with all shortfalls listed and escalated.

checklist.step: Compute the CRVM / Valuation Manual reserve on the same in-force
actions: Run the statutory reserve calculation per cohort — Commissioners Reserve Valuation Method on the applicable CSO table and calendar-year valuation interest rate for pre-Valuation-Manual issues, and the VM-20 net premium reserve with deterministic and stochastic reserves for issues subject to principle-based reserving.

Run the VM-20 stochastic and deterministic exclusion tests where they are claimed and print the test results and margins, because a failed exclusion test changes the reserve basis for the whole cohort.
Produce the reserve split by Exhibit 5 line — life insurance, annuities, supplementary contracts with life contingencies, accidental death benefit, disability active lives and disabled lives.
Export per-certificate reserves on the same certificate key as the nonforfeiture output so the two can be joined without a fuzzy match.
checklist.done: per-certificate statutory reserves exist on the nonforfeiture key, split by Exhibit 5 line, with exclusion test results printed.

checklist.step: Apply the cash-value floor test
actions: Join reserves to cash surrender values on certificate number and duration and compute calculated reserve minus cash surrender value for every certificate.
Set the held reserve to the greater of the calculated reserve and the cash surrender value and total the uplift separately so the floor effect is visible instead of buried in the aggregate.
List every certificate where the floor bites by more than 5% of the calculated reserve and investigate whether the driver is a mis-assigned nonforfeiture basis rather than a genuine floor.
Record the total floor uplift by plan code and Exhibit 5 line on the valuation control sheet and report it to the Appointed Actuary before the numbers are released.
checklist.done: held reserve is at least the cash surrender value for every certificate and the floor uplift is quantified by plan code and Exhibit 5 line.

checklist.step: Test for and compute deficiency reserves
actions: For each plan code compare the gross premium actually charged to the valuation net premium on the minimum reserve basis at every duration.

Where the gross premium is lower, compute the deficiency reserve as the present value of the future premium shortfall on the valuation basis, applying X-factors only where anticipated mortality experience supports them under the Valuation Manual.
Document each X-factor with its experience study reference, the credibility measure used and the study date, and have the Chief Actuary approve the factor set.
Add the deficiency reserve into the Exhibit 5 total and disclose it as a separate line on the valuation control sheet.
checklist.done: every plan code has a documented gross-versus-net premium test and any deficiency reserve is computed, X-factor supported and separately disclosed.

checklist.step: Run the reserve roll-forward and analysis of change
actions: Build the roll-forward: opening reserve, plus new issues, plus tabular interest and net premiums, less tabular cost, death and surrender releases, plus or minus floor and deficiency movement, equals closing reserve.
Reconcile the closing figure to the model output to the cent and attribute any residual to a named driver — never to a line called 'other'.
Compare movement in guaranteed cash values quarter on quarter by plan code and flag any plan where values moved without a matching in-force or duration change.
Send the roll-forward with a one-page commentary on the three largest drivers to the Valuation Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the roll-forward reconciles to the model closing reserve with every movement attributed to a named driver.

checklist.step: Tie reserve totals to Exhibit 5 and the general ledger
actions: Load the reserve totals into the annual statement software and populate Exhibit 5 by valuation standard, the Exhibit 5 interrogatories and Exhibit 7 for deposit-type contracts.

Reconcile the Exhibit 5 total to Page 3 Line 1 (Aggregate reserve for life contracts) and to the reserve control accounts in the general ledger, and post any true-up journal with the Controller before the ledger closes.
Run the annual statement software cross-checks and clear every Exhibit 5 fatal and warning edit, recording the resolution against each edit number.
Sign a tie-out sheet showing model total, Exhibit 5 total and ledger balance side by side with each reconciling item named.
checklist.done: Exhibit 5, Page 3 Line 1 and the ledger reserve balance agree, all statement validation edits are cleared and the tie-out is signed.

checklist.step: Document any change in the basis of valuation
actions: Identify every cohort whose mortality table, interest rate, valuation method or reserving approach changed since the prior year end.
Compute the reserve on both the old and the new basis for that cohort and record the difference, which is the figure reported in the change-in-valuation-basis disclosure of the annual statement.
Write the rationale — statutory amendment, Valuation Manual change, correction of an error, or voluntary strengthening — and cite the governing provision by section.
Route the change to the Chief Actuary for written approval before it is reflected, since an unapproved basis change is itself an exception.
checklist.done: every basis change is quantified on old and new bases, carries a cited rationale and has dated Chief Actuary approval.

checklist.step: Close model change control and version the run
actions: Compare the model version used for the run against the approved version register and confirm every code or assumption change since the last run carries an approved change ticket.
Confirm the validation report covering the nonforfeiture routine is current and that every high-rated validation finding is closed or has a documented compensating control.
Attach the run log, input hashes, parameter file and output control totals to the model governance record for the valuation date.
Capture the ASOP 56 model-governance attestation from the model owner that the model is fit for the nonforfeiture and reserving purpose it was used for.
checklist.done: the run is versioned in the model governance repository with approved change tickets, a current validation report and a model-owner attestation.

checklist.step: Peer review the valuation workpapers before release
actions: Read the cohort table, rate worksheet, worked adjusted-premium examples, floor test and roll-forward as one set rather than signing the summary alone.
Re-derive one adjusted premium and one minimum cash surrender value by hand for the largest plan code and compare the result to the model output.
Challenge in writing any plan code whose floor uplift, deficiency reserve or basis change moved materially against the prior quarter and require a written answer before sign-off.
Sign and date the valuation control sheet — this is the gate that releases the numbers to Statutory Reporting.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has hand-derived at least one value, cleared every challenge and signed the dated valuation control sheet.

checklist.step: File the valuation workpaper pack for the retention period
actions: Assemble the pack: frozen extract hash, cohort table, rate worksheet, model run log and version tag, per-certificate minimum value and reserve extracts, floor test, deficiency test, roll-forward, Exhibit 5 tie-out and signed control sheet.
File it under Valuation / REG-010 / <valuation date> and apply the life-of-block-plus-7-years retention label so it survives block runoff.
Confirm the pack is indexed and retrievable by valuation date, writing company NAIC co-code, plan code and situs state so an examiner request can be served without rebuilding the run.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager that the pack is filed and give them the repository reference.
checklist.done: the complete workpaper pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by valuation date, company, plan code and state.

testing.step: Build the population of certificates carrying guaranteed nonforfeiture values
actions: Extract every Group Life certificate in the quarter-end valuation file with a non-zero guaranteed cash value, plus the deposit-type contracts reported in Exhibit 7, split by writing company NAIC co-code, plan code, issue-year cohort and situs state.
Reconcile the extract row count and total face amount to the valuation control sheet totals and to Exhibit 5 by valuation standard, and resolve every difference before drawing a sample.
Add certificates that terminated during the quarter by surrender, lapse or death so the population cannot be trimmed to the surviving in-force only.
Sign the population as complete, recording extract date, row count and the reconciling items cleared.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to Exhibit 5 and the valuation control sheet, includes in-quarter terminations and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the valuation extract to the policy administration system of record
actions: Re-run an independent count and face-amount query against the Policy Administration Platform as at the valuation date and compare it to the frozen extract hash and control totals.
Test that the posting freeze held by searching for transactions posted into the valuation-date period after the extract timestamp.
Walk issue date, issue age, sex indicator, face amount and paid-to date for 25 certificates from the policy admin screens to the extract fields.
Treat any difference in issue date or issue age as a high-severity finding — both change the governing CSO table and the adjusted premium.
testing.done: the frozen extract agrees to an independently run source query and a 25-certificate field walk shows no unexplained differences.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible recalculation sample
actions: Take 100% of plan codes where the cash-value floor bit or a deficiency reserve was held, and 100% of cohorts with a change in valuation basis this period.
Draw 40 certificates at random with a recorded seed, stratified so every issue-year cohort and CSO table in force is represented at least twice.
Record population size, seed, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn identically by a third party.
Add every certificate on the prior quarter's exception list as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is seeded, reproducible, covers every CSO cohort and carries all prior-period exceptions as retest rows.

testing.step: Independently recalculate the minimum nonforfeiture value for each sampled certificate
actions: Build a standalone recalculation workbook that takes issue date, issue age, sex basis, face amount and gross premium and applies the governing CSO table plus a nonforfeiture interest rate derived independently as 125% of the calendar-year valuation interest rate rounded to the nearest 0.25%.

Compute the present value of future guaranteed benefits, the present value of future adjusted premiums and the statutory expense allowance from first principles, importing no intermediate value from the actuarial modeling platform.
Compare the recalculated minimum cash surrender value, paid-up value and extended term period to the model output and record the difference in dollars and percent.
Flag any certificate differing by more than $1, and any plan code differing by more than 0.1% in aggregate, as an exception.
Save the workbook with live formulas rather than pasted values so the independent reviewer can trace every cell.
testing.done: each sampled certificate has a first-principles recalculation in a live-formula workbook with the difference to the model quantified.

testing.step: Verify each cohort's nonforfeiture basis against the approved form filing
actions: For each sampled certificate open the approved filing in SERFF Filing Access by writing company NAIC co-code, state and form number and read the actuarial memorandum's stated nonforfeiture basis.
Compare the filed mortality table, interest rate, age basis and nonforfeiture method to the cohort assignment actually used in the valuation.
Check the state-specific approvals where Alabama, Arizona, California or Connecticut required a variation from the domiciliary basis and confirm the valuation honoured that variation.
Record any mismatch as a filed-versus-valued basis exception and capture the SERFF tracking number and disposition date as evidence.
testing.done: every sampled cohort's valuation basis matches its approved filing, with SERFF tracking numbers captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the cash-value floor test across the whole population
actions: Run an independent query joining the per-certificate reserve extract to the per-certificate cash surrender value extract and count every row where held reserve is less than cash surrender value.
Confirm the count is zero; any row returned is a reportable statutory breach rather than a test exception and is escalated to the Appointed Actuary the same day.
Recompute the total floor uplift from the query and agree it to the figure recorded on the valuation control sheet.
Check that terminated certificates were not excluded by the join in a way that hides a pre-surrender deficiency.
testing.done: the independent query returns zero certificates with reserve below cash surrender value and the floor uplift agrees to the control sheet.

testing.step: Trace printed contract guarantees to the statutory minimum for the sample
actions: Pull the issued certificate or master group contract for each sampled certificate and read the Table of Guaranteed Values exactly as printed.
Compare the printed value at durations 5, 10 and 20 to the independently recalculated statutory minimum for the same duration.

Confirm the printed default nonforfeiture option and the deferral language match the statute, including the insurer's right to defer payment of cash surrender values for up to six months after request.
Log any printed guarantee below the statutory minimum as a policyholder-impacting exception with an estimated affected certificate count and dollar impact.
testing.done: printed guarantees at three tested durations meet or exceed the recalculated statutory minimum, or the shortfall is logged with an impact estimate.

testing.step: Recompute the interest-rate derivation and the roll-forward arithmetic
actions: Independently derive the calendar-year statutory valuation interest rate from the published Moody's Corporate Bond Yield Average and confirm the company's rate worksheet reproduces it.
Recompute the nonforfeiture rate as 125% of that rate rounded to the nearest 0.25% and compare it to the rate actually loaded into the model parameter file.
Re-add the reserve roll-forward line by line and confirm opening plus movements equals the closing Exhibit 5 total to the cent.
Confirm the Exhibit 5 total agrees to Page 3 Line 1 and to the general ledger reserve control account balance.
testing.done: the independently derived rates match the model parameters and the roll-forward foots to Exhibit 5, Page 3 Line 1 and the ledger.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception recording certificate or plan code, states affected, dollar deficiency and whether policyholder values are impacted.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — wrong CSO table for the issue year, stale interest rate, extract field defect, model version drift, filed-versus-valued basis mismatch — and name an owner in Actuarial.
Set a remediation date inside the current quarter and, where a policyholder value was understated, open a value true-up and customer notification workstream with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open item into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row and report anything policyholder-impacting to the Appointed Actuary immediately.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an Actuarial owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the recalculation test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sample and compare results to the stated thresholds — zero floor breaches, $1 per certificate and 0.1% aggregate recalculation tolerance.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and ran none of the valuation models for the period, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open statutory breach to the Chief Actuary and to the Audit Committee at its next sitting, then file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alabama Standard Nonforfeiture Law (Ala. Code Tit. 27 Ch. 15) for the minimum-value floor the opinion asserts, plus the Standard Valuation Law and VM-30 (Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Requirements) of the current NAIC Valuation Manual for the opinion wording; each non-domiciliary state's minimum aggregate reserve requirement is re-read against the current Arizona, California and Connecticut nonforfeiture statutes before the scope paragraph is finalised

In-scope processes.value: Annual preparation, peer review and signature of the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, the supporting Actuarial Memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary for the Group Life and group permanent reserves reported in Exhibit 5 and the deposit-type contracts in Exhibit 7

In-scope systems.value: Opinion text is attached to the annual statement in the statutory reporting software; the memorandum, reliance letters and peer review are held in the compliance evidence repository with restricted access

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Audit Committee on appointment of the Appointed Actuary and re-approved annually in the December committee cycle, together with any VM-30 wording change published in the new Valuation Manual edition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Opinion signed and attached to the annual statement by March 1; the Actuarial Memorandum and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary completed by March 15; the VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report for principle-based cohorts by April 1

Deadline reminders configured.value: Opinion calendar alerts at December 1 (appointment and qualification confirmed), January 15 (reliance letters requested), February 10 (draft opinion to peer reviewer), February 24 (board notification) and March 10 (memorandum and RAAIS final)

checklist.step: Confirm the Appointed Actuary appointment is current and recorded by the board
actions: Pull the board or board-committee resolution appointing the Appointed Actuary and confirm it names the individual, the effective date and the writing companies covered.
Where the appointment changed during the year, confirm the notification to the domiciliary commissioner was made within the required period and hold the acknowledgement.
Check the resolution has not lapsed and covers the statement year being opined on, not just the current calendar year.
File the resolution reference into the opinion evidence pack and send it to the Appointed Actuary and the Chief Actuary by December 1.
checklist.done: a current board resolution naming the Appointed Actuary and the covered companies is in the opinion evidence pack, with any change-of-actuary notification acknowledged.

checklist.step: Document the Appointed Actuary's qualification to sign
actions: Record membership of the American Academy of Actuaries and the specific basic-education, experience and continuing-education requirements met under the U.S. Qualification Standards for a life statement of actuarial opinion.
Log continuing education hours for the year, split into relevant technical, professionalism and bias topics, with the activity names and dates.
Confirm no disciplinary matter or conflict of interest affects the appointment and record the confirmation in writing.
File the qualification statement in the opinion evidence pack, since an examiner will ask for it before reading the opinion itself.
checklist.done: a dated qualification statement with continuing education detail and a conflict declaration is filed in the opinion evidence pack.

checklist.step: Fix the scope of the opinion and the amounts it will cover
actions: List in the scope table every reserve and related actuarial item to be opined on: Exhibit 5 aggregate reserve for life contracts by valuation standard, Exhibit 5 interrogatories, Exhibit 7 deposit-type contracts, claim reserves in Exhibit 8 and any liability held under a reinsurance treaty.
Take the amounts directly from the statutory reporting software rather than from an actuarial summary so the scope table cannot drift from the filed statement.
Mark each scope line as covered by asset adequacy analysis or excluded, and state the reason for any exclusion.
Circulate the scope table to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Controller for confirmation that no reserve line has been left out.
checklist.done: the scope table lists every actuarial liability with amounts taken from the filed statement and each line marked as tested or excluded with a reason.

checklist.step: Collect the data reliance statement from the responsible company officer
actions: Send the reliance request to the officer responsible for policy administration data naming the exact extracts relied on, their as-of date and their record counts.
Require the officer's signed statement that the in-force and claim data supplied is substantially accurate and complete for the purpose of the actuarial opinion, in the form VM-30 contemplates.
Attach the extract hash and control totals from the valuation control sheet to the reliance letter so the letter is tied to identifiable data.
Chase and escalate to the Chief Financial Officer if the signed letter is not back by January 31 — the opinion cannot cite an unsigned reliance.
checklist.done: a signed, dated officer reliance statement naming the specific data extracts and their control totals is held in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Collect the asset and investment reliance statements
actions: Request from Investment Operations the year-end asset listing supporting the Group Life reserves: book value, market value, NAIC designation, maturity, cash-flow characteristics and any embedded options.
Reconcile the listing to Schedule D and Schedule DA totals in the annual statement and clear differences with the Investment Operations Manager.
Obtain the Chief Investment Officer's signed reliance statement covering asset data accuracy and the reinvestment and disinvestment strategy assumed in the analysis.
File the listing, the reconciliation and the signed reliance in the opinion evidence pack.
checklist.done: asset data is reconciled to Schedule D and covered by a signed investment reliance statement in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Assemble the evidence that reserves meet the nonforfeiture minimum floor
actions: Take the cash-value floor test output from the quarterly valuation and confirm no certificate holds a reserve below its statutory minimum cash surrender value at the statement date.

Produce the summary by plan code and issue-year cohort showing the governing CSO table, the nonforfeiture interest rate and the aggregate floor uplift, so the opinion's minimum-value assertion has a named source.
Note any nonforfeiture deficiency found during the year, the strengthening booked and the date it was booked.
Hand the pack to the Appointed Actuary with a cover note stating explicitly that the Standard Nonforfeiture Law minimum is met at the statement date.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary holds a dated pack evidencing that every certificate's reserve meets or exceeds its statutory minimum nonforfeiture value.

checklist.step: Test the minimum aggregate reserve requirement for every state of filing
actions: Build a state grid of the 51 jurisdictions the statement is filed in and record each state's minimum reserve and nonforfeiture standard where it differs from the Alabama domiciliary standard.
Recompute aggregate reserves on each differing state's minimum standard and compare to the reserve actually held.

Where a state's minimum exceeds the held reserve, quantify the additional reserve required and escalate it to the Chief Actuary before the opinion is drafted, because the opinion asserts sufficiency in every state of filing.
Record the grid and its conclusion as a named exhibit in the actuarial memorandum.
checklist.done: a 51-jurisdiction grid shows the held reserve is at least each state's minimum standard, with any shortfall quantified and escalated.

checklist.step: Draft the opinion using the prescribed wording for the applicable opinion type
actions: Start from the current VM-30 prescribed language and build the identification, scope, reliance and opinion paragraphs in the required order rather than editing last year's file.

State in the opinion paragraph that the reserves and related actuarial items make good and sufficient provision, are computed in accordance with commonly accepted actuarial standards and meet the requirements of the laws of every state in which the statement is filed — including the minimum nonforfeiture values required by the Standard Nonforfeiture Law.
Select the opinion type (unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive) and, if anything other than unqualified, write the specific reason and the amount involved into the opinion text.
Insert the reliance paragraphs naming each person relied on, their title and the subject of the reliance, matching the letters collected.
Check every amount quoted in the opinion against the scope table and the filed statement page and line.
checklist.done: a complete draft opinion exists with identification, scope, reliance and opinion paragraphs in the prescribed order and every amount tied to the filed statement.

checklist.step: Draft the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Build the memorandum sections VM-30 requires: description of the business covered, reserve methods and bases by cohort, assumptions and their support, the asset adequacy analysis approach, results, sensitivity tests and the actuary's conclusions.

Include the nonforfeiture exhibit — CSO table by issue-year cohort, nonforfeiture interest rate derivation and the cash-value floor result — so a reviewing actuary can follow the minimum-value assertion without a second request.
Cross-reference every number in the memorandum to a workpaper in the compliance evidence repository by reference id.

Mark the memorandum confidential on every page consistent with the Valuation Manual's confidentiality provisions and restrict repository access to the Actuarial function, the Chief Financial Officer and Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: the memorandum covers every VM-30 required section, cross-references its workpapers and is marked and access-restricted as confidential.

checklist.step: Prepare the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary
actions: Summarise the material issues from the asset adequacy analysis: scenarios producing negative results, the reserve or additional actuarial reserve held in response, and the changes in assumptions or methods from the prior year.
Compare the current year's asset adequacy conclusion to the prior year's and explain any movement in the additional reserve held.
State the extent to which the Appointed Actuary relied on other experts and on company data.
Have the Chief Actuary review the summary, then set it for delivery to the domiciliary commissioner by March 15.
checklist.done: the RAAIS is drafted, reviewed and scheduled for delivery to the domiciliary commissioner by March 15.

checklist.step: Obtain an independent peer review of the opinion and memorandum
actions: Give the reviewing actuary the draft opinion, the memorandum, the scope table, the nonforfeiture floor pack and the reliance letters as a complete set.

Require the reviewer to check the opinion type against the evidence, verify the amounts tie to the filed statement, and challenge any assumption whose support is a prior-year study without a recency check.
Log every review comment with the drafter's response and the resulting change to the text.
Require the reviewer's written statement that the review is complete and the comments are cleared before signature.
checklist.done: a documented peer review with every comment cleared and a written completion statement is held in the evidence pack.

checklist.step: Clear the opinion and memorandum through Regulatory Counsel
actions: Read the opinion wording against the current statutory and Valuation Manual requirements for the domiciliary state and confirm the required assertions are present and unmodified.
Confirm the confidentiality treatment claimed over the memorandum is available in each state that may request it and record where it is not.
Where the opinion is anything other than unqualified, agree the disclosure wording and the notification approach to the domiciliary commissioner.
Record counsel clearance with a date on the opinion routing sheet.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the opinion wording and the confidentiality position with a dated entry on the routing sheet.

checklist.step: Report the opinion outcome to the Board Audit Committee
actions: Table the opinion type, the scope amounts, the nonforfeiture floor conclusion, the asset adequacy result and any additional reserve held at the February Audit Committee.
Disclose every issue that could have qualified the opinion and the action taken to resolve it before signature.
Record the committee's acknowledgement in the minutes and load the paper into the board portal for the record.
Escalate immediately to the Chief Financial Officer and the committee chair if a qualification or adverse opinion is in prospect rather than waiting for the meeting.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has been given the opinion type, scope amounts and issues, and its acknowledgement is minuted.

checklist.step: Sign the opinion and attach it to the annual statement
actions: Sign and date the opinion in the Appointed Actuary's own name with title, employer, address and the date of signature, and record the qualification statement reference.
Attach the signed opinion to the annual statement in the statutory reporting software as the Statement of Actuarial Opinion for each writing company covered.

Re-check that the reserve amounts printed in the opinion equal the filed Exhibit 5 total and Page 3 Line 1 after any late statement change — a late journal entry after signature invalidates the opinion.
Confirm the signature date is on or before March 1 and freeze the opinion file against further edits.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion is attached to each company's annual statement, ties to Page 3 Line 1 and is frozen against edits by March 1.

checklist.step: File the opinion evidence pack and set the retention
actions: Assemble the pack: board resolution, qualification statement, scope table, reliance letters, nonforfeiture floor pack, state minimum grid, memorandum, RAAIS, peer review, counsel clearance, committee minute reference and signed opinion.
File it under Actuarial Opinion / REG-010 / <statement year> with a 7-year retention label and restricted access for the memorandum and RAAIS.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by statement year and writing company NAIC co-code so an examination request can be served without reassembly.
Notify Regulatory Reporting that the signed opinion is available for the state filing step.
checklist.done: the complete opinion evidence pack is filed, access-restricted, retention-labelled and retrievable by year and company.

testing.step: Assemble the population of opinions, memoranda and reliances for the statement year
actions: List every writing company that filed an annual statement for the year and confirm one signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion exists for each.
List each opinion's memorandum, RAAIS and every reliance letter cited in its reliance paragraphs.
Reconcile the company list to the statutory reporting software filing register so no company with a filed statement is missing an opinion.
Record the population with dates of signature and the opinion type for each company.
testing.done: every filed statement has a matched signed opinion, memorandum, RAAIS and reliance set, reconciled to the filing register.

testing.step: Check the opinion against the prescribed wording paragraph by paragraph
actions: Take the current VM-30 prescribed opinion language and tick off the identification, scope, reliance and opinion paragraphs one at a time against the signed text.
Confirm the opinion states that reserves meet the requirements of the laws of every state in which the statement is filed and that minimum nonforfeiture values are provided for.
Confirm the opinion type matches the evidence — an unqualified opinion sitting over an unresolved reserve shortfall is a fail, not a wording issue.
Record any missing or modified required paragraph as an exception with the exact text quoted.
testing.done: every required paragraph is present and unmodified, or the deviation is quoted and logged as an exception.

testing.step: Tie the scope amounts in the opinion to the filed annual statement
actions: Open the filed annual statement and read Exhibit 5 by valuation standard, Exhibit 7 and Page 3 Line 1 for each company.
Compare each figure to the corresponding amount in the opinion scope table and in the memorandum, with zero tolerance for difference.
Check the statement version compared is the one actually filed, including any amendment filed after March 1.
Investigate any post-signature journal entry affecting reserves and confirm whether the opinion was re-signed.
testing.done: every scope amount agrees exactly to the filed statement and any post-signature reserve movement is identified and resolved.

testing.step: Verify the appointment and qualification of the signing actuary
actions: Read the board resolution and confirm the signatory is the appointed individual for the statement year and for each company opined on.
Read the qualification statement and confirm the continuing education hours and topic split satisfy the U.S. Qualification Standards for this type of opinion.
Where the appointment changed in the year, confirm the notification to the domiciliary commissioner and hold the acknowledgement.
Treat a signature by an individual with no current appointment as a critical finding reportable to the Audit Committee immediately.
testing.done: the signatory is the board-appointed actuary for every company opined on, with documented qualification and any change notified.

testing.step: Re-perform the nonforfeiture minimum-value assertion on a sample
actions: Draw 30 certificates at random with a recorded seed across the plan codes named in the memorandum's nonforfeiture exhibit, weighted to the largest issue-year cohorts.
Recalculate each certificate's statutory minimum cash surrender value from first principles on its governing CSO table and nonforfeiture interest rate.
Compare the recalculated minimum to the reserve actually held at the statement date and confirm the reserve is not lower.
Report any certificate failing the floor directly to the Chief Actuary and the Audit Committee chair, since it contradicts a signed opinion.
testing.done: 30 recalculated certificates confirm the reserve held is at least the statutory minimum, or any failure is escalated as contradicting the opinion.

testing.step: Test the reliance letters actually support the reliances claimed
actions: Match each reliance paragraph in the opinion to a signed letter from the named individual with the stated title.
Check each letter names the specific data or analysis relied on, the as-of date and the control totals or extract identifiers rather than giving a generic assurance.
Confirm every letter is dated on or before the opinion signature date.
Trace one data reliance letter's control totals to the valuation control sheet and to the policy administration extract that fed the valuation.
testing.done: every claimed reliance has a specific, pre-dated, signed letter and one traced letter agrees to the valuation extract control totals.

testing.step: Test the memorandum and RAAIS for completeness and timing
actions: Check the memorandum contains every VM-30 required section, including the description of business, reserve bases, assumptions and their support, and the actuary's conclusions.
Confirm the memorandum was completed by March 15 and the RAAIS delivered to the domiciliary commissioner by March 15, using the repository timestamps and the delivery acknowledgement.
Sample five numbers in the memorandum and trace each to the referenced workpaper in the evidence repository.
Confirm the confidentiality marking and repository access restriction are in place on both documents.
testing.done: the memorandum is complete, timely, traceable on a five-number sample and correctly access-restricted, with the RAAIS delivery acknowledged.

testing.step: Verify the peer review was genuinely independent and its comments cleared
actions: Confirm the reviewing actuary did not prepare the memorandum, run the valuation models or author the nonforfeiture exhibit.
Read the comment log and check every comment has a drafter response and, where a change was agreed, a corresponding change in the final text.
Confirm the reviewer's completion statement is dated before the opinion signature date.
Flag any review that consists only of a sign-off sheet with no comments as an ineffective control.
testing.done: the peer review is independent, dated before signature, and every comment traces to a response and a text change.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the company, the opinion element affected and whether it changes the opinion type or the filed reserve.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — missing reliance, stale wording carried from the prior year, scope amount drift after a late journal, qualification documentation gap, unresolved nonforfeiture shortfall — and an owner in Actuarial or Statutory Reporting.

Set a remediation date before the next statement cycle and, where the filed opinion is affected, agree with Regulatory Counsel whether an amended filing or a notification to the domiciliary commissioner is required.
Carry every open item into next year's opinion readiness review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a decision on whether the regulator must be notified.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the opinion review
actions: Compare the results to the stated thresholds — every required paragraph present, every reliance supported, scope amounts tying exactly to the filed statement, zero nonforfeiture floor failures.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the reviewer, who is outside Actuarial and had no part in drafting or peer reviewing the opinion, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Board Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns delivery of the signed actuarial opinion with the annual statement to the NAIC and all 51 jurisdictions; the Appointed Actuary owns only the content of the opinion being filed

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alabama's Standard Nonforfeiture Law and Standard Valuation Law filing requirements as administered by ALDOI, plus the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions (Life, Accident & Health) and the per-jurisdiction NAIC State Filing Checklist, which is re-read each January because states change between electronic-only and electronic-plus-hard-copy for the actuarial opinion

In-scope processes.value: Annual statement assembly and filing for each writing company: jurat page execution, attachment of the Statement of Actuarial Opinion, NAIC Financial Data Repository submission, per-state filing to all 51 jurisdictions, filing fee payment and receipt capture

In-scope systems.value: Annual statement software produces the filing package and the NAIC transmission; per-state filing status, confirmations and fee receipts are tracked in the Internal Regulatory System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Statement & Actuarial Opinion Filing Procedure — jurat execution, opinion attachment control, state-by-state checklist build, NAIC electronic submission, hard-copy states, fee payment, confirmation capture and the 51-jurisdiction completeness reconciliation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and reviewed each January against the newly published NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and the refreshed state filing checklists

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual statement and Statement of Actuarial Opinion due March 1 to the NAIC and every state of licensure; risk-based capital filing March 1; supplemental filings April 1; the actuarial memorandum and RAAIS held ready for the domiciliary commissioner from March 15

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at February 1 (state checklist refresh complete), February 20 (jurat signatures obtained), February 26 (NAIC submission dry run), March 1 (submission cut-off) and March 8 (all 51 confirmations captured)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed statement PDF per company, the attached signed opinion, the NAIC submission confirmation, per-state confirmations or postal proof of delivery, and fee receipts, retained 7 years from the filing date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any jurisdiction filed after March 1, any state where the opinion was omitted from the package, and any rejected or resubmitted filing is logged with the state, the days late, the cause and the penalty or fine assessed

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Financial Officer signs off any late or amended annual statement filing and any correspondence to a commissioner explaining a missed or defective filing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every writing company × jurisdiction filing obligation for the statement year — the full 51-jurisdiction grid per company — plus each amended filing made after the original submission

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any jurisdiction with no filing confirmation on or before March 1, or any filing package that omits the signed actuarial opinion, is a fail; the opinion attached must be the signed version, and a draft or unsigned attachment counts as an omission

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with a hard March 1 date; the test runs once in March over the complete 51-jurisdiction grid for every company, with a November readiness check of the state checklist refresh

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared, transmitted or confirmed any of the filings being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual filing completeness workpaper (51-jurisdiction grid per company with confirmation reference, timestamp and opinion-attachment check) in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Reporting / REG-010

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filing confirmation register showing, per company and jurisdiction, the submission timestamp, confirmation reference and the opinion attachment identifier — producible to any department that queries receipt within 2 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting answers filing-receipt and completeness queries directly from the confirmation register; anything questioning the content of the opinion is routed to the Appointed Actuary, and any late-filing penalty notice goes to Regulatory Counsel and the Chief Financial Officer

checklist.step: Refresh the per-jurisdiction filing requirements before the season opens
actions: Download the current NAIC State Filing Checklist for Life, Accident & Health for the statement year and read the column for each of the 51 jurisdictions covering the annual statement, the actuarial opinion and the supplements.

Record per jurisdiction: electronic-only versus electronic-plus-hard-copy, whether the actuarial opinion must be filed in original signed form, the filing fee amount and payment channel, and any state-specific form or cover letter.
Compare the new checklist to the prior year's grid and highlight every change so a state that moved from electronic to hard copy is not missed.
Load the refreshed grid into the Internal Regulatory System as the filing plan and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager approve it by February 1.
checklist.done: an approved 51-jurisdiction filing grid for the statement year exists with channel, fee, opinion format and changes-from-prior-year flagged.

checklist.step: Confirm the annual statement is final and the reserves are locked
actions: Confirm the general ledger is closed for the statement year and no further journal entries affecting Exhibit 5, Exhibit 7 or Page 3 Line 1 will be posted.
Run the annual statement software's full validation suite and clear every fatal and warning cross-check, recording the resolution against each edit number.
Reconcile Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 7 totals to the Appointed Actuary's scope table and obtain written confirmation from the Appointed Actuary that the figures match the opinion.
Freeze the statement version and record the version identifier that will be filed.
checklist.done: the statement is validated, frozen and confirmed by the Appointed Actuary to match the amounts in the opinion.

checklist.step: Attach the signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion to each company's package
actions: Retrieve the signed opinion PDF from the compliance evidence repository and check the signature, date and the writing company name on its face before attaching it.
Attach it in the annual statement software as the Statement of Actuarial Opinion for the correct company and statement year.
Open the assembled package and read the attachment back to confirm it is the signed version, not a draft, and that all pages are present and legible.
Record the attachment file name and hash against the company row in the filing grid.
checklist.done: each company's package carries the correct signed opinion, verified page by page, with its file hash recorded in the filing grid.

checklist.step: Execute and notarise the jurat page
actions: Route the jurat page for the required officer signatures — typically the president, the secretary and the treasurer or their equivalents — for each writing company.
Have the signatures notarised where the jurisdiction or the statement instructions require it and check the notary block is complete and dated.
Verify the officer names and titles on the jurat match the current officer register held for the company.
Return the executed jurat to Regulatory Reporting and file the original in the corporate records.
checklist.done: an executed, correctly notarised jurat page with officers matching the register exists for every writing company.

checklist.step: Submit the annual statement filing to the NAIC
actions: Generate the NAIC electronic filing files for each writing company and run a dry-run submission by February 26 to surface format rejections while there is still time.
Submit the annual statement, the attached actuarial opinion and the required supplements to the NAIC Financial Data Repository under the company's NAIC co-code and group code.
Capture the NAIC submission confirmation, including the timestamp and confirmation reference, and paste it against the company row in the filing grid.
Resolve any NAIC validation rejection the same day and re-submit; a rejected submission is not a filing.
checklist.done: each company has an accepted NAIC submission with a captured timestamp and confirmation reference, and no open rejections.

checklist.step: File to each domiciliary and non-domiciliary state per its channel
actions: For electronic-only jurisdictions confirm the NAIC submission satisfies the state and record the state's reliance on the NAIC filing in the grid.
For jurisdictions requiring a direct submission, upload the package to that department's portal or send the required hard copy with an original signed opinion, using tracked delivery.
Send the Alabama Department of Insurance filing first as the domiciliary state and confirm receipt before working through the remaining 50 jurisdictions.
Record the submission date, channel, reference number and tracking number against every jurisdiction row.
Escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager any jurisdiction whose portal is unavailable, so an alternative channel can be used before March 1.
checklist.done: all 51 jurisdictions show a recorded submission with date, channel and reference, with the domiciliary filing confirmed first.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fees and capture receipts
actions: Take the fee schedule per jurisdiction from the filing grid and raise the payments through the required channel, whether a state portal, an EFT to the department or a cheque with the hard-copy filing.
Match each payment to the jurisdiction row and record the payment reference and the cleared date.
Chase any payment that has not cleared within 10 business days, since an unpaid fee can leave a filing recorded as incomplete.
Reconcile total fees paid to the fee schedule and post the accrual reversal with the Controller.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction's filing fee is paid, referenced against its grid row and reconciled to the fee schedule.

checklist.step: Capture and file every filing confirmation
actions: Collect the NAIC confirmation, each state portal acknowledgement, each email receipt and each delivery tracking proof for hard-copy states.
File them in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Reporting / REG-010 / <statement year> / <company> / <jurisdiction>.
Update the filing grid status to Confirmed only when a confirmation artefact exists — a sent-items email is not a confirmation.
Chase any jurisdiction still unconfirmed at March 8 by telephoning the department's financial analysis contact and logging the call.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction row carries a filed confirmation artefact, with unconfirmed states chased and the calls logged.

checklist.step: Run the 51-jurisdiction completeness reconciliation
actions: Compare the licensed-jurisdiction list for each writing company, taken from the licence register, to the filing grid so no state of licensure is missing a row.
Confirm every row shows submission date on or before March 1, a confirmation reference and an opinion attachment identifier.
List any gap and treat it as a live filing failure requiring same-day action rather than a reporting note.
Sign the reconciliation and circulate it to the Chief Financial Officer and the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation shows every licensed jurisdiction filed on time with a confirmation and an opinion attachment.

checklist.step: Hold the memorandum and RAAIS ready for the domiciliary commissioner
actions: Confirm with the Appointed Actuary that the actuarial memorandum is complete by March 15 and the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary has been delivered to ALDOI.
Record the RAAIS delivery date, channel and acknowledgement in the filing grid alongside the opinion row.
Keep the memorandum access-restricted and ready to produce on request without a rebuild, with the confidentiality marking intact.
Diarise the VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report for April 1 where principle-based cohorts are in force.
checklist.done: the memorandum is complete and access-restricted, the RAAIS delivery is acknowledged and recorded, and the April 1 PBR report is diarised.

checklist.step: Handle rejections, resubmissions and amended filings
actions: Log every rejection or department request for correction with the jurisdiction, the reason given and the date received.
Rework the package, obtain any re-signature the change requires — a change to a reserve amount requires the Appointed Actuary to re-sign the opinion — and resubmit through the same channel.
Record the amended filing as a new grid row rather than overwriting the original, so the original and amended timeline is visible to an examiner.
Notify the Chief Financial Officer of any amendment that changes a filed reserve amount.
checklist.done: every rejection or amendment is logged, reworked with any required re-signature, resubmitted and recorded as a distinct grid row.

checklist.step: Track and answer state financial-analysis follow-ups on the filing
actions: Log every department query about the filing — missing supplement, unreadable attachment, mismatch between the opinion and Exhibit 5 — with the date received and the department's stated due date.
Route content questions on reserves or nonforfeiture values to the Appointed Actuary and keep the drafting and clock-tracking with Regulatory Reporting.
Answer within the department's stated period, defaulting to 30 days where none is stated, and capture the response and the department's closure.
Escalate any query alleging a deficient filing to Regulatory Counsel before responding.
checklist.done: every department query is logged with its due date, answered within the period and closed with the department's acknowledgement captured.

checklist.step: Report filing completion to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare a one-page filing status report showing companies filed, jurisdictions confirmed, any late filing with its days late, and any penalty assessed.
Table it at the March management meeting and at the next Audit Committee, with the signed completeness reconciliation attached.
Record the acknowledgement in the minutes and load the paper into the board portal.
Raise any repeat late jurisdiction as a control deficiency requiring a named remediation owner.
checklist.done: filing completion, lateness and penalties are reported and minuted, with repeat lateness raised as a control deficiency.

checklist.step: Close the filing season and update the grid for next year
actions: Record for each jurisdiction what actually worked — channel used, portal quirks, contact names, lead time needed — as a note on the grid row.
Flag jurisdictions whose requirements changed mid-season so the February checklist refresh starts from the correct baseline.
Diarise the next statement year's milestones in the filing calendar with the same alert points.
Archive the completed grid as the statement year's filing record.
checklist.done: the completed grid is archived with per-jurisdiction operating notes and next year's milestones are diarised.

checklist.step: File the filing evidence pack and set the retention
actions: Assemble per company: filed statement PDF, attached signed opinion, executed jurat, NAIC confirmation, all 51 jurisdiction confirmations, fee receipts, amendment records and the signed completeness reconciliation.
File it under Regulatory Reporting / REG-010 / <statement year> with a 7-year retention label from the filing date.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by statement year, writing company NAIC co-code and jurisdiction, which is how an examiner will ask for it.
Notify the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Appointed Actuary that the season's evidence is closed and filed.
checklist.done: the per-company filing evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by year, company and jurisdiction.

testing.step: Build the population of company × jurisdiction filing obligations
actions: Extract the licence register for every writing company and list each jurisdiction in which it is licensed for the statement year.
Cross the list with the statement year to produce the complete obligation grid and count the expected filings.
Reconcile the licence register to the NAIC company profile and to the premium tax filings so a jurisdiction with premium but no filing obligation row is caught.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date and the expected filing count.
testing.done: the obligation grid is built from the licence register, reconciled to premium tax filings and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the obligation grid to actual confirmations
actions: Match every obligation row to a confirmation artefact in the evidence repository — NAIC confirmation, state portal acknowledgement or delivery proof.
List rows with no artefact, with a sent-items email only, or with a confirmation dated after March 1 as automatic exceptions.
Confirm the confirmation names the same writing company and statement year as the obligation row.
Quantify total unmatched rows before any sampling begins.
testing.done: every obligation row is matched to a dated confirmation artefact or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible jurisdiction sample
actions: Take 100% of hard-copy and non-standard-channel jurisdictions and 100% of jurisdictions that changed requirements this season.
Draw 20 further jurisdictions at random with a recorded seed across the remaining rows, covering every writing company at least twice.
Record the population size, seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every jurisdiction that filed late in the prior year as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is seeded, reproducible, covers all non-standard channels and includes prior-year late jurisdictions.

testing.step: Open each sampled filing package and verify the opinion attachment
actions: Retrieve the actual package filed for each sampled jurisdiction rather than the master package held internally.
Open the Statement of Actuarial Opinion attachment and confirm it is signed, dated on or before March 1, names the correct writing company and is complete and legible.
Compare the attachment hash to the hash recorded on the filing grid row.
Treat an unsigned, draft or missing opinion as an omission and therefore a fail, not a documentation issue.
testing.done: every sampled package contains the correct signed opinion, hash-matched to the filing grid record.

testing.step: Re-perform the timeliness computation against the March 1 deadline
actions: Read the submission timestamp from each sampled confirmation in the department's own time zone, not the company's.
Compute days late as submission date minus March 1 and record zero or a positive number for every row.
Check whether the jurisdiction operates a different statutory due date and, where it does, recompute against that date and record the source.
List any positive day count as an exception and quantify any penalty assessed or expected.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed per sampled jurisdiction against the correct statutory date, with days late and penalties quantified.

testing.step: Verify the opinion filed matches the opinion signed by the Appointed Actuary
actions: Retrieve the master signed opinion from the Actuarial evidence pack and compare it page for page with the version filed in each sampled jurisdiction.
Compare the reserve amounts stated in the opinion to Exhibit 5 and Page 3 Line 1 in the filed statement for that company.
Confirm the minimum nonforfeiture value assertion appears in the filed text and was not truncated by the packaging process.
Log any version difference as a critical exception, since different states holding different opinion texts is itself a reportable condition.
testing.done: the filed opinion is identical to the signed master in every sampled jurisdiction and its amounts tie to the filed statement.

testing.step: Test the jurat execution and fee payment on the sample
actions: Check the jurat page in each sampled filing carries the required officer signatures, correct titles per the officer register and a complete notary block where required.
Trace the filing fee for each sampled jurisdiction to a payment record and a cleared date in the general ledger.
Confirm the fee amount matches the state's published schedule for the statement year.
Flag any unpaid or short-paid fee, which can leave the filing recorded by the department as incomplete.
testing.done: every sampled filing has a properly executed jurat and a cleared fee payment matching the published schedule.

testing.step: Test the memorandum and RAAIS delivery to the domiciliary commissioner
actions: Confirm from the repository timestamp that the actuarial memorandum was complete by March 15 for every writing company.
Trace the RAAIS delivery to ALDOI to an acknowledgement, with the delivery date and channel recorded.
Confirm the memorandum's confidentiality marking and access restriction survived the delivery and the repository filing.
Where a principle-based cohort is in force, confirm the VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report was delivered by April 1.
testing.done: memorandum completion, RAAIS delivery and any VM-31 report are evidenced against their March 15 and April 1 dates.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the company, the jurisdiction, what was missed and whether the department has raised it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — stale state checklist, portal failure not escalated, opinion attached unsigned, fee unpaid, late statement close — and an owner in Regulatory Reporting.
Set a remediation date and, for any late or defective filing, agree with Regulatory Counsel whether a proactive letter to the commissioner is required.
Carry every open item into the next filing season's readiness check as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a decision on regulator notification.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing completeness test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the obligation grid against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed jurisdictions and omitted opinions.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared or transmitted none of the filings, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any late jurisdiction and any penalty to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
