checklist.step: Define the asset segments supporting the Group Life liabilities
actions: Agree with the Chief Investment Officer which investment segment backs the Group Life and group permanent reserves and record the segment identifier used in the investment system.
Confirm the segment's assets are formally allocated in the accounting records rather than notionally assigned, and document the allocation method where assets are shared.
Record the segmentation basis — book value matched to reserve, or a stated allocation percentage — and the date it was last reviewed.
Have the Appointed Actuary approve the segment definition before any modelling starts, since re-segmenting mid-cycle invalidates comparability.
checklist.done: the backing asset segment is defined, formally allocated, documented and approved by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Source and reconcile the asset data and its cash flows
actions: Extract from the investment system, for every holding in the segment: CUSIP, book and market value, NAIC designation, coupon, maturity, call and put features, prepayment characteristics and amortisation schedule.
Reconcile the extract's total book value to Schedule D Part 1 and Schedule DA for the segment and clear differences with Investment Operations before use.
Generate the projected asset cash flows on the base scenario and check they reproduce the current book yield within a stated tolerance.
File the extract, the Schedule D reconciliation and the cash-flow generation log in the AAT evidence pack.
checklist.done: segment asset data is extracted, reconciled to Schedule D and Schedule DA, and its base-scenario cash flows reproduce the book yield.

checklist.step: Build and reconcile the liability model points
actions: Compress the Group Life valuation in-force into liability model points grouped by plan code, issue-year cohort, issue age band, sex basis and guaranteed cash value level.
Reconcile model point face amount, statutory reserve and guaranteed cash value totals back to the valuation output and to Exhibit 5, requiring agreement within 0.5% on each measure.
Run a seriatim-versus-compressed comparison on one plan code to prove the compression does not distort the guaranteed cash value profile that drives surrender behaviour.
Record the reconciliation and the compression test in the AAT evidence pack and have the Valuation Actuary confirm it.
checklist.done: liability model points reconcile to Exhibit 5 within 0.5% on face, reserve and cash value, with a documented compression test.

checklist.step: Set and support the assumption basis
actions: List every assumption used — mortality, base lapse, dynamic lapse, premium persistency, expense, expense inflation, reinvestment strategy, disinvestment order, default costs and spread — and name the study or source behind each.
Check each supporting experience study is dated within three years and, where it is older, write the rationale for continuing to rely on it.
State the margin for adverse deviation applied to each assumption and how it was set, rather than describing the assumption as best estimate with no margin discussion.
Route the assumption set with its support to the Appointed Actuary for approval before the September cycle opens.
checklist.done: every assumption has a named, dated source, a stated margin and Appointed Actuary approval before the cycle opens.

checklist.step: Model the surrender and cash-value election behaviour the nonforfeiture guarantees create
actions: Build the dynamic lapse formula so surrender rates respond to the gap between the guaranteed cash surrender value available under the Standard Nonforfeiture Law and prevailing market alternatives in the scenario.
Model the nonforfeiture options a certificate holder can actually elect — cash surrender, reduced paid-up and extended term insurance — and the value payable under each, not cash surrender alone.
Reflect the insurer's statutory right to defer payment of cash surrender values for up to six months and state whether the deferral is assumed to be exercised.
Run a sensitivity doubling the dynamic lapse response and record the effect on ending surplus, since disintermediation against guaranteed values is the central risk this block carries.
Document the formulas, their parameters and the sensitivity in the AAT report.
checklist.done: surrender modelling responds to the guaranteed nonforfeiture values, covers all elective options and carries a documented double-response sensitivity.

checklist.step: Construct the deterministic scenario set
actions: Build the seven prescribed deterministic interest rate scenarios — level, uniformly increasing, increasing then popping down, pop-up then level, uniformly decreasing, decreasing then popping up, and pop-down then level — from the statement-date Treasury curve.
Source the starting curve and credit spreads from the market data terminal on the valuation date and record the exact quotes used.
Add any company-specific scenario the prior year's results or the current risk profile call for, and explain why it was added.
File the scenario definitions and starting curve in the AAT evidence pack so an examiner can reproduce them.
checklist.done: the seven prescribed scenarios plus any added scenario are defined from a recorded statement-date curve and filed.

checklist.step: Generate and validate the stochastic scenario set
actions: Generate the stochastic economic scenarios using the prescribed generator and record the version, parameters, seed and number of paths.
Run the calibration checks on the generated set and confirm the distribution meets the prescribed calibration criteria at the tested percentiles.
Confirm the scenario count is sufficient for the tail measure being used and document the convergence test that supports it.
File the seed and generator configuration so the identical set can be regenerated on request.
checklist.done: the stochastic set is generated with a recorded seed, passes calibration checks and has a documented convergence test.

checklist.step: Run the projections and control the run
actions: Confirm the model version tag matches the version approved in the model governance repository and that the asset and liability input files match the reconciled extracts by hash.
Run the deterministic set first and check the level scenario reproduces the prior-year roll-forward within the stated tolerance before launching the stochastic run.
Capture the run log, run duration, error and warning messages, and confirm no model point dropped between input and output.
Export results by scenario: ending surplus, the year it first turns negative if it does, and the present value of accumulated deficiency.
checklist.done: runs complete on the approved model version with hash-matched inputs, no dropped model points and per-scenario results exported.

checklist.step: Interpret the results and identify failing scenarios
actions: Rank scenarios by ending surplus and list every scenario ending in deficiency, with the first year of deficiency and the driver.
Separate deficiencies driven by interest rate movement from those driven by surrender behaviour against guaranteed cash values, because the two call for different responses.
Compare the pattern to the prior year and explain every material change in conclusion.
Record the adequacy conclusion per segment in writing before any additional reserve is computed, so the reserve is a response to a documented conclusion rather than a plug.
checklist.done: failing scenarios are listed with first-deficiency year and driver, and a written per-segment adequacy conclusion exists.

checklist.step: Determine and book any additional actuarial reserve
actions: Compute the additional actuarial reserve on the stated basis — commonly the greatest present value of accumulated deficiency across the tested scenarios — and show the calculation.
Confirm the resulting total reserve still satisfies the Standard Nonforfeiture Law cash-value floor at certificate level, since an aggregate additional reserve does not cure a seriatim floor failure.
Instruct the Statutory Reporting Manager to book the reserve to the correct Exhibit 5 line and confirm it flows to Page 3 Line 1.
Document the rationale, the scenario it responds to and the release conditions in the AAT report and the memorandum.
checklist.done: any additional actuarial reserve is computed, shown, booked to Exhibit 5 and documented with its rationale and release conditions.

checklist.step: Run and document the required sensitivities
actions: Run sensitivities on mortality, base and dynamic lapse, expense inflation, reinvestment spread and default cost, one factor at a time, and record the ending surplus movement for each.
Run a combined adverse sensitivity and record whether the block remains adequate under it.
Identify the two assumptions the result is most sensitive to and state what monitoring is in place for them during the year.
Present the sensitivity table in the AAT report next to the base results rather than in an appendix.
checklist.done: single-factor and combined sensitivities are run and tabled, with the two dominant assumptions named and their monitoring stated.

checklist.step: Roll the September testing forward to the year-end position
actions: Compare the December 31 in-force, reserves and asset segment to the September 30 basis on which the testing was run and quantify each change.

Assess whether any change — a large new group, a block transfer, a market move, a reinvestment strategy change — invalidates the September conclusion, and re-run rather than reason around it if it does.
Document the roll-forward test and its conclusion and have the Appointed Actuary sign it by February 15.
Update the additional actuarial reserve for the year-end position where the roll-forward shows it is required.
checklist.done: the September conclusion is tested against the December 31 position, signed by the Appointed Actuary, with the reserve updated where needed.

checklist.step: Write the asset adequacy testing report
actions: Write the report to stand alone for a reviewing actuary: segment definition, asset and liability data and reconciliations, assumptions and their support and margins, scenario definitions, results, sensitivities, roll-forward and conclusion.
Include the nonforfeiture linkage explicitly — how guaranteed cash surrender values enter the liability cash flows and drive the dynamic lapse response.
Cross-reference every table to its underlying workpaper by reference id so a request for support does not trigger a rebuild.
Mark the report confidential consistent with the memorandum and restrict repository access accordingly.
checklist.done: a self-contained, cross-referenced, confidentiality-marked AAT report exists covering data, assumptions, scenarios, results and conclusion.

checklist.step: Close model governance on the testing cycle
actions: Confirm the cash-flow model version used is the approved version and that every change since the last cycle carries an approved change ticket and test evidence.
Confirm the model validation covering the asset and liability projection engines is current and that high-rated findings are closed or compensated.
Attach run logs, input hashes, scenario seeds and result exports to the model governance record for the cycle.
Record the ASOP 56 attestation from the model owner covering fitness for the asset adequacy purpose.
checklist.done: the cycle is versioned in model governance with approved changes, a current validation, attached run evidence and a model-owner attestation.

checklist.step: File the AAT evidence pack and set the retention
actions: Assemble the pack: segment definition, asset extract and Schedule D reconciliation, liability model points and compression test, assumption set with studies, scenario definitions and seeds, run logs, results, sensitivities, roll-forward, additional reserve calculation and the signed AAT report.
File it under Asset Adequacy / REG-010 / <statement year> with a 7-year retention label and restricted access.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by statement year, segment and writing company NAIC co-code.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager that the pack supporting the opinion and the RAAIS is filed.
checklist.done: the complete AAT evidence pack is filed, access-restricted, retention-labelled and retrievable by year, segment and company.

testing.step: Build the population of segments, model points and scenarios tested
actions: List every asset segment supporting Group Life reserves and confirm each appears in the AAT report with a stated conclusion.
List the liability model point files, the deterministic scenario set and the stochastic scenario set with its seed and path count.
Reconcile the segments listed to the investment system's segment register and the reserves covered to Exhibit 5, so no reserve is left untested.
Sign the population as complete with the reconciling items cleared.
testing.done: every segment and reserve in Exhibit 5 is covered by a tested segment with a stated conclusion, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile asset and liability inputs back to the systems of record
actions: Re-run an independent book value total for the segment from the investment system and compare it to the asset file used in the model and to Schedule D Part 1.
Compare liability model point totals for face amount, statutory reserve and guaranteed cash value to the valuation output and Exhibit 5, testing against the 0.5% threshold.
Confirm the file hashes recorded in the run log match the reconciled extracts actually filed in the evidence pack.
Treat any difference above threshold, or any hash mismatch, as an exception before proceeding to result testing.
testing.done: asset and liability inputs agree to Schedule D and Exhibit 5 within 0.5% and the run-log hashes match the filed extracts.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible sample of assumptions and scenarios
actions: Take 100% of assumptions the sensitivity table shows the result is most sensitive to, and 100% of scenarios that ended in deficiency.
Draw 10 further assumptions and 5 further scenarios at random with a recorded seed.
Record the population size, seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every assumption flagged in the prior year's review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is seeded and reproducible and covers all dominant assumptions and all deficiency scenarios.

testing.step: Test the support behind each sampled assumption
actions: Open the experience study cited for each sampled assumption and check its date, exposure period, credibility measure and whether it covers the Group Life block rather than a different line.
Compare the assumption actually loaded into the model parameter file to the value the study supports and record any difference.
Check the stated margin for adverse deviation exists in the parameter file, not only in the narrative.
Treat an assumption supported only by a prior-year assumption document, with no underlying study, as unsupported.
testing.done: each sampled assumption traces to a dated, relevant study whose supported value and margin match the model parameter file.

testing.step: Re-perform the dynamic lapse and nonforfeiture-option modelling
actions: Take the dynamic lapse formula from the model and recompute the surrender rate independently at three scenario points — level rates, sharply rising rates and sharply falling rates.
Confirm the formula reacts to the guaranteed cash surrender value available under the Standard Nonforfeiture Law and not only to a credited-rate differential.
Confirm reduced paid-up and extended term elections are modelled with the correct values from the nonforfeiture output rather than approximated as cash surrender.
Recompute the six-month deferral assumption's effect and confirm the report states whether deferral is assumed to be exercised.
testing.done: the recomputed dynamic lapse matches the model at three scenario points and all nonforfeiture elections are modelled with their correct values.

testing.step: Re-run a sampled scenario and compare to the recorded result
actions: Restore the archived model version, input files and scenario definition for one deterministic and one stochastic path from the model governance record.
Re-run the projection and compare ending surplus, first year of deficiency and present value of accumulated deficiency to the recorded results.
Investigate any difference beyond floating-point tolerance as evidence that the archived configuration does not reproduce the reported result.
Record the re-run log and comparison in the workpaper as the reproducibility evidence an examiner will ask for.
testing.done: an archived re-run reproduces the recorded scenario results within tolerance, with the run log filed as reproducibility evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the additional actuarial reserve and check the nonforfeiture floor still holds
actions: Recompute the additional actuarial reserve on the stated basis from the exported scenario results and compare it to the amount booked.
Trace the booked amount to the Exhibit 5 line and to Page 3 Line 1 in the filed statement.

Re-run the certificate-level cash-value floor test on the year-end position to confirm the aggregate additional reserve did not mask a seriatim shortfall against the statutory minimum nonforfeiture value.
Log any difference between recomputed and booked amounts, and any seriatim floor failure, as separate exceptions.
testing.done: the additional reserve recomputes to the booked amount, ties to Exhibit 5 and no seriatim nonforfeiture floor failure exists.

testing.step: Test the roll-forward from the testing date to the statement date
actions: Compare the September 30 in-force, reserve and asset segment used in testing to the December 31 filed position and quantify the change independently.
Assess whether any change exceeded the company's own re-run trigger and, if it did, confirm a re-run actually happened.
Confirm the roll-forward conclusion is signed by the Appointed Actuary and dated on or before February 15.
Check the market movement between the testing date and the statement date was considered explicitly, not assumed immaterial.
testing.done: the roll-forward is independently quantified, re-run triggers were honoured and the signed conclusion pre-dates February 15.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the segment, the assumption or scenario affected and whether it changes the adequacy conclusion or the additional reserve.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — stale experience study, model version drift, input reconciliation break, dynamic lapse formula not tied to guaranteed values, roll-forward trigger ignored — and an owner in Actuarial or ALM.
Set a remediation date before the next testing cycle opens in September and, where the adequacy conclusion is affected, notify the Appointed Actuary the same day.
Carry every open item into next cycle's assumption approval as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where relevant, same-day notification to the Appointed Actuary.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the asset adequacy review
actions: Compare results to the stated thresholds — 0.5% input reconciliation, every deficiency scenario reserved, every material assumption supported by a study within three years.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who built no part of the model and set none of the assumptions, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Appointed Actuary, the Chief Risk Officer and the Audit Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Confirm the extract specification against the current policy admin release
actions: Read the release notes for every policy administration release deployed since the last valuation and list any change to fields the nonforfeiture calculation depends on — issue date, issue age basis, sex indicator, plan code, face amount, paid-to date, guaranteed cash value and policy loan.
Confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead whether any plan code was added, retired or remapped in the quarter and how historic certificates were treated.
Update the extract specification and its field mapping document, and have the Valuation Actuary confirm the mapping still delivers what the model expects.
Publish the specification version that will govern this quarter's extract.
checklist.done: the extract specification is versioned for the quarter and reflects every policy admin change touching a nonforfeiture-relevant field.

checklist.step: Run the extract under the posting freeze and publish control totals
actions: Trigger the valuation extract job only after the Policy Admin Ops Lead confirms the posting freeze for the valuation date, and record the freeze time in the job parameters.
Land the extract in Snowflake Data Cloud in a valuation-date partition marked read-only and compute the file hash.
Publish control totals — record count, total face amount, total guaranteed cash value, total policy loan balance — to the reconciliation dashboard the same day.
Fail the job rather than land a partial file if the row count deviates from the prior quarter by more than 5% without a known driver.
checklist.done: a hashed, read-only extract is landed for the valuation date with published control totals and no partial-load condition.

checklist.step: Tie record count and face amount to the system of record
actions: Run an independent count and sum query directly against the policy administration replica as at the valuation date, using the same in-force definition as the extract.
Compare record count (must tie exactly) and total face amount (must tie within 0.1%) and list every difference with its certificate numbers.
Classify each difference — timing, in-force definition, status code mapping, genuine omission — and resolve rather than net them off against each other.
Record the tie-out on the reconciliation report with the queries used pasted in full.
checklist.done: record count ties exactly and face amount ties within 0.1%, with every difference identified and classified rather than netted.

checklist.step: Run the nonforfeiture-critical field rule set
actions: Execute the completeness rules: issue date, issue age, sex or composite indicator, plan code and face amount must be populated on every row, with zero tolerance.

Execute the validity rules: issue date not in the future and not before the plan's launch date, issue age within the plan's issue age range, sex indicator in the permitted value list, plan code present in the product reference data, face amount above the plan minimum.
Execute the consistency rules: issue age must agree with issue date and date of birth on the certificate's age basis, and paid-to date must not pre-date the issue date.
Route every failure into the exception register with severity Critical for the fields that determine the governing CSO table and the adjusted premium.
checklist.done: completeness, validity and consistency rules have run over every row with failures registered and severity-rated.

checklist.step: Reconcile the guaranteed cash value field to the product's value table
actions: Join each certificate's stored guaranteed cash value to the plan's Table of Guaranteed Values at the certificate's duration and compare.
List every certificate where the stored value differs from the table value by more than $1, since a stored-value defect flows straight into the statutory floor test.
Distinguish genuine defects from legitimate differences caused by policy loans, partial surrenders or paid-up additions and document the distinction rule.
Send the difference list to the Valuation Actuary and the Policy Administration Analyst the same day.
checklist.done: every stored guaranteed cash value is compared to the product value table with differences listed and their cause classified.

checklist.step: Reconcile the in-force movement quarter on quarter
actions: Build the movement: opening certificate count and face amount, plus new issues and reinstatements, less deaths, surrenders, lapses, maturities and conversions, equals closing.
Tie the movement counts to the policy administration transaction history for the quarter rather than to a status-code snapshot difference.
Investigate every unexplained variance above $250,000 of face amount and name the driver — a status change without a transaction usually means a data fix was applied directly to the database.
Record the movement table on the reconciliation report with each variance named.
checklist.done: the movement reconciles from opening to closing against transaction history with every variance above $250,000 named.

checklist.step: Test for duplicate, orphan and out-of-scope certificates
actions: Search for duplicate certificate numbers within a master policy and duplicate person-plus-plan combinations that indicate a double load.
Search for certificates with no valid master policy, no writing company NAIC co-code or no situs state — these cannot be assigned a jurisdiction's nonforfeiture standard.
Search for certificates whose situs state is outside the 51 jurisdictions the company is licensed in and escalate them to Compliance rather than dropping them.
Register every hit as an exception with its certificate numbers rather than filtering it out of the extract.
checklist.done: duplicates, orphans and out-of-jurisdiction certificates are identified, registered and escalated rather than silently filtered.

checklist.step: Tie cash value payments and policy loans to the general ledger
actions: Sum the cash surrender payments recorded in policy administration for the quarter and compare to the surrender benefit expense accounts in the general ledger.
Compare the extract's total policy loan balance to the policy loan asset account and to Schedule B or the equivalent statement line.
Investigate suspense and unapplied cash for surrender payments that were processed but not disbursed, since an unpaid surrender is a policyholder-value issue, not just a reconciliation break.
Record the tie and any reconciling item on the reconciliation report and clear it with the Controller before the ledger closes.
checklist.done: surrender payments and policy loan balances tie to the ledger, with suspense items identified and cleared with the Controller.

checklist.step: Disposition every exception with severity and impact
actions: Work the exception register top down by severity, taking every Critical exception affecting the nonforfeiture basis fields first.
For each exception set the disposition: corrected at source in policy administration, corrected by a documented valuation adjustment, or accepted for this quarter with a quantified reserve impact.
Quantify the reserve and cash-value impact of every accepted exception rather than describing it as immaterial, and name the accepting owner.
Refuse to close any Critical exception by acceptance without the Valuation Actuary's written agreement.
checklist.done: every exception carries a disposition, a quantified impact where accepted, and written Valuation Actuary agreement on Critical items.

checklist.step: Push permanent fixes back into the policy administration system
actions: Raise a data correction ticket per source defect with the certificate numbers, the field, the correct value and its supporting document.
Apply the correction through the system's maintenance transaction so the change is audited, never by a direct database update.
Confirm the correction re-flows to the next extract and closes the corresponding rule failure.
Where the defect is systemic — a broken interface, a bad conversion, a defective release — raise a change request rather than repeating the manual fix each quarter.
checklist.done: source defects are corrected through audited transactions and systemic causes have a raised change request, not a recurring manual fix.

checklist.step: Produce the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Assemble the report: extract specification version and hash, control totals and source tie-out, rule set results by severity, guaranteed cash value comparison, movement reconciliation, ledger tie and the exception register with dispositions.
Show quarter-on-quarter trend on exception counts by rule so a deteriorating field is visible before it becomes a valuation problem.
State plainly which exceptions remain open and their quantified reserve impact, on the front page rather than in an appendix.
Circulate to the Valuation Actuary, the Chief Data Officer and the Statutory Reporting Manager on WD+2.
checklist.done: the reconciliation report is issued on WD+2 with tie-outs, rule results, trends and open exceptions with quantified impact on the front page.

checklist.step: Obtain the Valuation Actuary's data acceptance
actions: Read the reconciliation report and challenge every open Critical exception before signing anything.
Sign the data acceptance stating the extract is fit for the nonforfeiture and reserve calculation, listing each accepted exception and its quantified impact.
Where acceptance is refused, hold the valuation run and escalate to the Chief Actuary and the Chief Data Officer the same day rather than running on known-bad data.
File the signed acceptance with the valuation control sheet so the two documents travel together.
checklist.done: a signed data acceptance listing every accepted exception and its impact is filed with the valuation control sheet, or the run is held.

checklist.step: Feed the accepted extract into the valuation model
actions: Point the model run at the accepted extract by hash, not by folder path, so a later re-landed file cannot be picked up silently.
Re-check model point count and face amount against the published control totals before the run is allowed to proceed.
Record the extract hash, the reconciliation report reference and the data acceptance reference in the model run log.
Stop the run and return to the Data Quality Manager if the model's own input validation raises a record the reconciliation did not.
checklist.done: the model run is bound to the accepted extract by hash with the reconciliation and acceptance references recorded in the run log.

checklist.step: Track recurring data defects to a root-cause fix
actions: Compare this quarter's exception register to the prior three quarters and list every rule failing repeatedly on the same field or plan code.
Assign each recurring defect a named data steward and a root-cause fix — interface repair, conversion clean-up, screen validation, reference data correction — with a target quarter.
Report recurring defects and their fix status to the Data Governance forum each quarter with the reserve impact attached.
Escalate any defect open for more than three quarters to the Chief Data Officer and the Chief Actuary.
checklist.done: every recurring defect has a named steward, a root-cause fix with a target quarter, and escalation after three quarters open.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation evidence pack and set the retention
actions: Assemble the pack: extract specification version, extract hash, source tie-out queries and results, rule set output, guaranteed cash value comparison, movement reconciliation, ledger tie, exception register with dispositions and the signed data acceptance.
File it under Data Quality / REG-010 / <valuation date> with a 7-year retention label.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by valuation date, writing company NAIC co-code and plan code so it can be produced alongside the valuation workpapers at an examination.
Notify the Valuation Actuary and the Statutory Reporting Manager of the repository reference.
checklist.done: the reconciliation evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable alongside the valuation workpapers.

testing.step: Build the population of records subject to reconciliation
actions: Take the full quarter-end valuation extract from its read-only partition and record its row count, total face amount and hash.
Take the in-quarter movement transactions — issues, reinstatements, deaths, surrenders, lapses, maturities, conversions — from the policy administration transaction history.
Confirm the extract partition is the one the model actually consumed by matching the hash in the model run log.
Sign the population as complete with the extract date, row count and hash recorded.
testing.done: the tested population is the hash-matched extract the model consumed, together with the quarter's movement transactions.

testing.step: Independently reconcile the extract to the policy administration system of record
actions: Write and run an independent in-force query against the policy administration replica as at the valuation date rather than re-running the company's own script.
Compare record count, face amount, guaranteed cash value total and policy loan total to the published control totals.
Investigate any difference the company's reconciliation did not report — an unreported difference is a control failure regardless of size.
Test that the posting freeze held by looking for transactions posted into the valuation period after the extract timestamp.
testing.done: an independently written query reproduces the control totals and no unreported difference or post-freeze posting exists.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible record sample
actions: Take 100% of certificates carrying a Critical exception and 100% of certificates involved in the movement variances named on the report.
Draw 40 certificates at random with a recorded seed, stratified across plan codes, issue-year cohorts and situs states.
Record population size, seed, stratification and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every certificate on the prior quarter's exception list as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is seeded, reproducible, stratified and includes all Critical exceptions and prior-quarter items.

testing.step: Walk each sampled record field by field from the source screen
actions: Open each sampled certificate in the policy administration system and read issue date, date of birth, issue age, sex indicator, plan code, face amount, paid-to date, guaranteed cash value and policy loan from the screen.
Compare each field to the extract row and record any difference with a screenshot.
Where the source screen and the underlying document disagree, open the issued certificate in the document repository and treat the document as the arbiter.
Treat any difference in issue date, issue age, sex basis or plan code as a Critical finding, since each changes the governing CSO table or the adjusted premium.
testing.done: each sampled record is walked field by field from the source screen with differences evidenced and Critical fields flagged.

testing.step: Re-run the nonforfeiture-critical rule set independently
actions: Re-execute the completeness, validity and consistency rules against the same extract partition using an independently held rule definition.
Compare the failure counts by rule to the counts on the company's reconciliation report and investigate any difference.
Test that a rule cannot pass a row it should fail by injecting three deliberately defective rows — a null issue date, an out-of-range issue age and an unknown plan code — into a test copy.
Record the rule coverage: any nonforfeiture-critical field with no rule attached is itself a finding.
testing.done: independently re-run rules reproduce the reported failure counts, catch injected defects and cover every nonforfeiture-critical field.

testing.step: Recompute the in-force movement and the ledger tie
actions: Rebuild the movement from opening to closing independently from the transaction history and compare each line to the company's movement table.
Recompute total cash surrender payments for the quarter and compare to the surrender benefit accounts in the general ledger.
Compare the extract's policy loan total to the policy loan asset balance and to the statement schedule.
Check suspense and unapplied cash for surrender payments processed but never disbursed and quantify the policyholder exposure.
testing.done: the movement rebuilds independently, surrender payments and loans tie to the ledger, and undisbursed surrenders are quantified.

testing.step: Test the disposition of every open and accepted exception
actions: Take the exception register and check each entry has a severity, a disposition and, where accepted, a quantified reserve and cash-value impact.
Confirm every Critical acceptance carries the Valuation Actuary's written agreement dated before the model run.
Recompute the impact of two accepted exceptions independently and compare to the figure recorded.
Treat 'immaterial' with no number behind it as an unsupported disposition and log it as an exception.
testing.done: every exception disposition is complete, Critical acceptances are pre-dated and signed, and two recomputed impacts agree.

testing.step: Confirm the model consumed the accepted extract and nothing else
actions: Read the model run log and compare the input file hash to the hash on the accepted extract and on the signed data acceptance.
Confirm the run started after the data acceptance was signed, not before.
Compare model point counts and face amount in the run's reconciliation report to the published control totals.
Treat any run on an unaccepted or re-landed extract as a control failure reportable to the Chief Actuary.
testing.done: the model run is proven to have consumed the hash-matched accepted extract, after acceptance, with counts agreeing to control totals.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per test exception naming the certificate or rule, the field affected and whether reserves or policyholder values are impacted.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — interface defect, conversion residue, missing screen validation, reference data gap, direct database update, freeze not honoured — and a named data steward.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and escalate anything affecting the governing nonforfeiture basis to the Valuation Actuary the same day.
Carry every open item into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, a named steward, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the reconciliation test
actions: Compare results to the stated thresholds — exact record count tie, 0.1% face and reserve tolerance, zero nulls or invalids in the nonforfeiture-critical fields, $250,000 movement variance limit.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who built neither the extract nor the rules and dispositioned no exception, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open Critical exception to the Chief Data Officer, the Chief Actuary and the Data Governance forum, and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the technical content of every response on Group Life reserves and nonforfeiture values; the Regulatory Reporting Manager owns intake, the response clock and transmission

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the inquiry is answered against the Standard Nonforfeiture Law of the asking jurisdiction (Alabama for domiciliary matters, Arizona, California or Connecticut where a non-domiciliary analyst asks) as it read on the date under review, plus the Standard Valuation Law, the Valuation Manual edition in force for that statement year, and the department's own authority to demand information

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven handling of every regulator contact touching Group Life valuation or nonforfeiture values: NAIC Financial Analysis Handbook Level 1 and Level 2 analyst letters, domiciliary financial analyst interrogatories, financial condition examination information requests, and non-domiciliary department queries following annual statement review

In-scope systems.value: Every inquiry, clock, owner, draft and transmission is tracked in the Internal Regulatory System; supporting calculations come from the archived valuation workpapers and are re-run in the actuarial modeling platform where a recomputation is demanded

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulator Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure — intake and authority check, classification and clock start, evidence assembly from archived workpapers, as-of-date reconstruction rule, confidentiality assertion, counsel and Appointed Actuary approval, transmission channel and correspondence file closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and Regulatory Counsel; reviewed after every financial condition examination cycle and whenever a department changes its inquiry channel or response window

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The department's own stated due date governs; where none is stated, respond within 30 calendar days of receipt, and within 10 business days for an examination information request during fieldwork, with an interim holding response inside 5 business days if the full answer will be late

Deadline reminders configured.value: Per-inquiry alerts at receipt+1 day (acknowledgement sent), at 50% and 80% of the elapsed window, at due date minus 3 business days (counsel and Appointed Actuary review complete) and on the due date itself, escalating to the Chief Financial Officer if unanswered

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The correspondence file — inbound letter, acknowledgement, working notes, supporting calculations, confidentiality assertion, approvals, the response as sent and the department's closure — retained 7 years from closure and produced at the next examination

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any inquiry answered after its due date, any response later corrected, and any inquiry that identifies a genuine reserve or nonforfeiture defect is logged with the jurisdiction, the days late or the defect amount, and the remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off every corrected response and every submission that concedes a reserve or nonforfeiture deficiency to a department

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every regulator inquiry touching valuation or nonforfeiture received in the period, from every jurisdiction and channel — department letter, analyst email, examination information request and telephone request subsequently confirmed in writing

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on lateness — any response sent after the department's due date without an agreed extension in writing is a fail; every factual assertion in a response must trace to an archived workpaper, and a response containing an unsupported number is a fail even if it was timely

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over all inquiries received or closed in the quarter, and 100% of examination information requests are tested at the close of each examination

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, approved or transmitted any of the responses being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulator inquiry test workpaper (inquiry register, clock recomputation, traceability sample, approval evidence) in the compliance evidence repository under Regulatory Inquiries / REG-010 / <quarter>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A per-inquiry correspondence file with the inbound request, the response as sent, the supporting calculation extract and the department's closure, producible on request within 2 business days and indexed by jurisdiction and inquiry date

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting acknowledges and controls the clock; the Appointed Actuary owns and approves the technical answer; Regulatory Counsel clears confidentiality assertions over the actuarial memorandum and any admission of deficiency before transmission

checklist.step: Take in the inquiry and open a correspondence file the day it arrives
actions: Log the inquiry the day it is received with jurisdiction, department contact name and title, channel, receipt date, statement year or valuation date referenced and the department's stated due date.
Attach the inbound letter, email or examination request exactly as received, including its attachments, without reformatting.
Where the request arrived by telephone, write a file note of what was asked and ask the department to confirm the request in writing before work starts.
Open the correspondence file under the jurisdiction and inquiry date so every later artefact lands in one place.
checklist.done: the inquiry is logged with jurisdiction, contact, receipt date and stated due date, and the original request is attached unaltered.

checklist.step: Confirm the requester's authority and the scope of what is being asked
actions: Confirm the sender is acting for a department with authority over the writing company in that jurisdiction, and check the company's licence status there.
Identify the authority relied on — routine financial analysis, examination authority, or a specific statutory demand — and record it on the file.
Mark any part of the request that reaches beyond that authority, in particular a demand for the actuarial memorandum from a jurisdiction where confidentiality protection is uncertain.
Give the Regulatory Reporting Manager a written scope note stating what will be answered, what will be answered under a confidentiality assertion, and what will be queried back.
checklist.done: the requester's authority is confirmed and a written scope note records what will be answered, protected or queried.

checklist.step: Classify the inquiry and start the response clock
actions: Classify as Level 1 analyst question, Level 2 analyst interrogatory, examination information request, or non-domiciliary statement query, since each carries a different turnaround expectation.
Set the due date to the department's stated date, or receipt plus 30 calendar days where none is stated, or receipt plus 10 business days for an examination request during fieldwork.
Configure the alerts at receipt+1 day, 50% and 80% elapsed, due minus 3 business days and the due date.
Name the responsible Actuarial owner and the Regulatory Reporting coordinator on the file the same day.
checklist.done: the inquiry is classified, its due date and alerts are set, and an Actuarial owner and coordinator are named.

checklist.step: Acknowledge receipt to the department
actions: Send a written acknowledgement within one business day naming the company, the NAIC co-code, the inquiry reference and the date the response will be delivered.
Ask the department to clarify anything ambiguous now rather than after the work is done — in particular the exact valuation date, the plan codes and the states in scope.
Name a single company contact for the inquiry so the department is not fielding parallel answers from Actuarial and Finance.
File the acknowledgement in the correspondence file.
checklist.done: a written acknowledgement naming the contact and the delivery date is sent within one business day and filed.

checklist.step: Retrieve the archived valuation evidence for the period under review
actions: Pull the workpaper pack for the exact valuation date referenced: frozen extract hash, cohort table, rate worksheet, adjusted-premium worked examples, cash-value floor test, roll-forward and Exhibit 5 tie-out.
Pull the matching data reconciliation pack and the signed data acceptance for the same date.
Pull the actuarial opinion, memorandum, RAAIS and AAT report for the statement year the inquiry concerns.
Check every pulled document is the version actually filed or signed and note the repository reference of each on the working note.
checklist.done: the archived valuation, reconciliation and opinion evidence for the referenced date is retrieved and version-checked with references recorded.

checklist.step: Answer as of the date under review, not as of today
actions: Establish the mortality table, nonforfeiture interest rate, valuation interest rate and Valuation Manual edition that governed on the date the inquiry concerns, and state them explicitly in the working note.
Reject any temptation to answer using the current basis — a nonforfeiture question about a 2015 issue is answered on the 2001 CSO basis then in force.
Where the basis has since changed, note the change and its date separately so the department sees the timeline rather than an apparent inconsistency.
Have the Chief Actuary confirm the as-of basis before any numbers are drafted.
checklist.done: the governing mortality table, interest rates and Valuation Manual edition as at the date under review are established and confirmed by the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Reproduce the calculation the department is questioning
actions: Restore the archived model version and input files by hash and re-run the specific certificates, plan codes or aggregates the department named.
Compare the re-run output to the originally reported figures and explain any difference before it is offered to the department.

Where the question is a minimum nonforfeiture value, produce a certificate-level worked calculation showing present value of guaranteed benefits, present value of adjusted premiums and the expense allowance components.
Save the re-run log, the restored input hashes and the worked calculation into the correspondence file as the support behind every number that will be sent.
checklist.done: the questioned calculation is reproduced from archived inputs, differences are explained and a worked certificate-level example is on file.

checklist.step: Draft the response so each answer sits under the department's own question
actions: Restate each numbered question from the department verbatim and put the answer directly beneath it, so nothing asked can be missed.
Give the number, the basis it was computed on and the workpaper reference for every figure quoted, rather than a narrative assurance.
Where the honest answer is that a defect exists, state it plainly with the amount, the affected certificate count, the states involved and the remediation already under way.
List the enclosures by name and mark which ones are provided under a confidentiality assertion.
Keep every claim inside what the archived evidence supports — nothing in the letter may rest on recollection.
checklist.done: a question-by-question draft exists in which every figure carries its basis and a workpaper reference, with enclosures listed.

checklist.step: Assert confidentiality over the memorandum and other protected material
actions: Identify every enclosure attracting confidential treatment — the actuarial memorandum, the RAAIS, the AAT report and any underlying experience study.
Prepare the confidentiality assertion letter citing the provision relied on in that jurisdiction and confirm the protection is actually available there.
Mark each protected page and record in the file which documents were released, to whom and under what protection.
Where a jurisdiction will not honour the protection, agree with the Appointed Actuary and the Chief Financial Officer what is released before anything is sent.
checklist.done: protected enclosures are identified, marked, covered by a jurisdiction-specific assertion, and any unprotectable release is agreed in advance.

checklist.step: Review the draft for accuracy and legal exposure
actions: Read the draft against the underlying workpapers and check every quoted number to its source, not to the summary that quoted it.
Challenge any sentence that concedes more than the evidence supports, and any that hedges a fact the evidence establishes.
Confirm the response answers every numbered question, including any the drafter judged already covered elsewhere.
Record the review comments and their resolution on the file before it goes to counsel.
checklist.done: every quoted number is traced to source, every question is answered and review comments are resolved on the file.

checklist.step: Obtain counsel clearance and the Appointed Actuary's approval to send
actions: Route the final draft with all enclosures to Regulatory Counsel and capture written clearance, in particular for any admission of a nonforfeiture or reserve deficiency.
Have the Chief Financial Officer approve any response that changes a filed reserve amount or foreshadows an amended annual statement.
Sign the response personally where it expresses an actuarial conclusion, since the department is relying on the Appointed Actuary's professional statement.
Record both approvals with dates on the file before transmission.
checklist.done: written counsel clearance and the Appointed Actuary's signed approval are on file, with CFO approval where a filed reserve is affected.

checklist.step: Transmit through the department's own channel and capture proof
actions: Send through the channel the department specified — its secure portal, the examination request system, or the named analyst's address — never a different channel because it is more convenient.
Capture the transmission timestamp, the portal reference or delivery receipt and the exact enclosure list as sent.
Compare the transmission timestamp to the due date and record days early or late on the file.
Send an interim holding response inside 5 business days of realising a full answer will be late, and ask for an extension in writing rather than letting the date pass.
checklist.done: the response is sent through the specified channel with proof of delivery captured and the timeliness recorded on the file.

checklist.step: Work the follow-ups and any examination information request list
actions: Log each follow-up question as a child item of the original inquiry with its own owner and due date rather than reopening the parent.

For a financial condition examination, keep the examiners' information request list as a live register with per-item status, owner and delivery date, and reconcile it to the examiners' own list weekly.
Hold a standing weekly call with the examiner-in-charge during fieldwork and minute what was requested and what was delivered.
Escalate to the Chief Financial Officer any request the company cannot meet in the time given, before the date rather than after.
checklist.done: every follow-up and examination request item has its own owner, due date and delivery record, reconciled weekly to the examiners' list.

checklist.step: Close the inquiry and record what it revealed
actions: Obtain the department's closure or no-further-questions confirmation and file it; an inquiry with no closure stays open on the register.

Where the inquiry exposed a genuine defect in reserves, nonforfeiture values or documentation, raise a tracker issue with the amount, owner and remediation date and link it to the correspondence file.
Record what the department actually asked about so recurring themes across jurisdictions are visible — repeated questions on the same topic usually mean the filed disclosure is unclear.
Report closed inquiries, open items and themes to the Chief Financial Officer monthly and to the Audit Committee quarterly.
checklist.done: the inquiry is closed with department confirmation, any defect is tracked to an owner, and themes are reported to management.

checklist.step: File the correspondence file and set the retention
actions: Assemble the file: inbound request, acknowledgement, scope note, retrieved workpaper references, re-run logs and worked calculations, draft and final response, confidentiality assertion, approvals, transmission proof, follow-ups and closure.
File it under Regulatory Inquiries / REG-010 / <jurisdiction> / <inquiry date> with a 7-year retention label from closure.
Confirm the file is retrievable by jurisdiction, statement year and inquiry date, which is how the next examination will ask for it.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and the Regulatory Reporting Manager of the repository reference.
checklist.done: the complete correspondence file is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by jurisdiction, statement year and inquiry date.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation-related regulator inquiries for the period
actions: Extract every inquiry logged in the quarter with jurisdiction, receipt date, classification, owner, due date and status.

Search the Appointed Actuary's, Chief Actuary's and Regulatory Reporting Manager's mailboxes and the examination portal for department correspondence that never reached the register — an unlogged inquiry is the most likely place a deadline was missed.
Add every open examination information request item as a population row in its own right.
Sign the population as complete with the sources searched and the unlogged items found.
testing.done: the population covers the register plus a mailbox and portal sweep, with any unlogged inquiry identified and counted.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the departments' own records where available
actions: For the domiciliary state and the two largest non-domiciliary states, compare the register to the correspondence held in the examination file and to any department acknowledgement list.
Confirm each inquiry's receipt date on the register matches the date on the inbound document rather than the date it was logged.
List every inquiry whose logged receipt date is later than the document date and quantify the clock time lost.
Treat a systematic lag between document date and logged date as a control finding, not an administrative note.
testing.done: register receipt dates are reconciled to inbound document dates with any logging lag quantified.

testing.step: Draw and document a reproducible inquiry sample
actions: Take 100% of inquiries answered late, 100% of inquiries that conceded a defect, and 100% of examination information request items delivered after their agreed date.
Draw 10 further inquiries at random with a recorded seed across jurisdictions and classifications.
Record population size, seed and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every inquiry flagged in the prior quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample is seeded, reproducible and includes all late, defect-conceding and prior-flagged inquiries.

testing.step: Recompute the response clock for each sampled inquiry
actions: Read the department's stated due date from the inbound document itself and recompute the deadline independently — stated date, or receipt plus 30 calendar days, or receipt plus 10 business days for examination fieldwork.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the transmission timestamp on the proof of delivery and compute days early or late.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm it was granted in writing by the department before the original date passed; a verbal or after-the-fact extension does not count.
Record every positive day count as an exception regardless of whether the department complained.
testing.done: each sampled inquiry has an independently recomputed deadline compared to the delivery proof, with any lateness quantified.

testing.step: Trace every number in the sampled responses to archived evidence
actions: Take each figure quoted in the response as sent and follow its workpaper reference into the archived valuation, reconciliation or AAT pack.
Confirm the figure in the workpaper matches the figure in the letter exactly and that the workpaper is the version in force at the date under review.
Flag any figure with no reference, or a reference to a document created after the response was sent, as an unsupported assertion.
Recompute one nonforfeiture value quoted in the sample from first principles to confirm the answer given to the department was correct.
testing.done: every quoted figure traces to a pre-existing archived workpaper and one recomputed nonforfeiture value confirms the answer given.

testing.step: Test that the answer was given on the basis in force at the date under review
actions: For each sampled inquiry, read the working note's statement of the governing mortality table, nonforfeiture interest rate and Valuation Manual edition.
Independently confirm those were the standards in force on the valuation date the department asked about, using the issue-year cohort rules.
Flag any response that used the current basis to answer a historic question, since it misrepresents the position to the department.
Confirm any subsequent change in basis was disclosed in the response with its effective date.
testing.done: each sampled response is confirmed to use the standards in force at the date under review, with later basis changes disclosed.

testing.step: Verify approvals, confidentiality assertions and the transmission channel
actions: Confirm each sampled response carries dated Regulatory Counsel clearance and the Appointed Actuary's approval before the transmission timestamp.
Where a filed reserve amount was affected, confirm the Chief Financial Officer's approval is also on file.
Check the confidentiality assertion cites the provision available in the receiving jurisdiction and that protected enclosures were marked.
Confirm the response went through the channel the department specified and that the delivery proof names the correct recipient.
testing.done: every sampled response has pre-dated approvals, a jurisdiction-correct confidentiality assertion and proof of delivery on the specified channel.

testing.step: Test that defects surfaced by inquiries were tracked and remediated
actions: For every sampled inquiry that identified a reserve, nonforfeiture or documentation defect, confirm a tracker issue exists with the amount, owner and remediation date.
Trace one remediation through to completion evidence — a booked reserve strengthening, a corrected policyholder value or an amended filing.
Confirm the department's closure was obtained after the remediation, not before it.
Flag any defect closed on the inquiry file with no corresponding tracker issue as a control failure.
testing.done: every defect surfaced by an inquiry has a tracker issue and one traced remediation is evidenced through to completion.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per test exception naming the jurisdiction, the inquiry, what failed and whether the department is aware.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — inquiry never logged, clock set from the logging date, answer given on the current rather than the historic basis, unsupported figure quoted, approval obtained after transmission, wrong channel used — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarter and, where a response was materially wrong, agree with Regulatory Counsel whether a corrected submission is required.
Carry every open item into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a decision on whether to correct the response.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the inquiry-handling test
actions: Compare results to the stated thresholds — zero responses after the department's due date without a written extension, and zero unsupported figures in a response.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper reference behind each element tested.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted, approved and transmitted none of the sampled responses, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion, any late response and any corrected submission to the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
